page: Google Cloud Platform a2-ultragpu-2g is an accelerator-optimized server featuring two NVIDIA Ampere A100 GPUs with a combined 160 GB of VRAM. The system is powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor providing 24 dedicated vCPUs across 12 physical cores operating at 2.2 GHz. It includes 340.0 GB of system memory, yielding 14.17 GB per core, and is equipped with 804 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between CPU-bound and GPU-accelerated workloads. Single-core CPU performance is weak, with stress-ng single-core scoring 1201.05 and Geekbench single-core scoring 1039.0, placing them in the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth fall into the average range, with a Passmark CPU score of 18766.4 and uncached read memory bandwidth at 93.72 GB/sec. Conversely, the server demonstrates top-tier performance in LLM inference benchmarks, achieving 500.14 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 24.17 tokens/sec for text generation on large 70B models, placing it in the top 10%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of GPU and memory resources makes this server a specialized asset. The tradeoff lies in the relatively modest CPU capabilities; paying for premium GPU hardware while running tasks that rely heavily on single-threaded CPU execution results in resource underutilization. However, for workloads that can offload computation to the dual A100 GPUs, the high throughput justifies the hardware class.

This server configuration is designed for large language model inference, deep learning training, and GPU-accelerated data science jobs. The combination of 160 GB of total VRAM and 804 GB of local NVMe SSD storage also supports complex simulation tasks and parallelized graphics rendering, while it is less suited for general-purpose web serving or CPU-bound compilation tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform a2-ultragpu-2g is an accelerator-optimized server designed for GPU-intensive workloads. It features two NVIDIA Ampere A100 GPUs with 160 GB of total VRAM, paired with 24 dedicated Intel Xeon vCPUs running at 2.2 GHz. The system includes 340.0 GB of RAM and 804 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Benchmark results show weak single-core CPU performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1039.0, and average multi-core capabilities. However, it excels in LLM inference, achieving top-tier results in prompt processing and text generation across small, medium, and large models. This hardware profile represents a high-density accelerator resource, making it highly efficient for deep learning and parallelized computation, though less cost-effective for CPU-bound tasks. It is best suited for large language model inference, data science, and GPU-accelerated simulations.
